prize_parts.citation: for the development of palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen bond formation, making aryl amines from aryl halides and amines a general and predictable reaction
for the development of base editing, programmable chemical conversion of DNA bases without double-strand cleavage

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B039 for Buchwald and Hartwig, B062 for Liu, three names in total. The round-1 exchange sharpened the case for B039 rather than weakening it. The chair asked whether the 2010 prize leaves C-N coupling a distinct principle. I think it does, and for a chemical reason: the 2010 reactions form C-C bonds from organometallic partners, and their key steps (transmetalation then reductive elimination) are well behaved. Forming C-N bonds from an amine and an aryl halide requires a different outcome from the catalytic cycle: amine binding and deprotonation at palladium, and then a C-N reductive elimination that is intrinsically slow and in competition with beta-hydride elimination and catalyst decomposition. It was solved by ligand design, in the 1990s by chelating bisphosphines and then by bulky biaryl and hindered alkyl phosphines, and the result is a general method. A concrete citation can be written around the C-N bond, which is what I propose. On chronology, which the chair asked for: Kosugi and Migita reported stoichiometric aryl bromide plus tin-amide coupling in 1983, Buchwald reported a catalytic version still dependent on aminostannanes in 1994, and Buchwald and Hartwig independently reported direct coupling of free amines with a base in 1995 and the following years. The 1983 work is a precursor to the idea; the method that chemists use came from the two groups. I do not credit Kosugi in the three-name set. For B062, I keep Liu alone. The deaminase-fusion principle for cytidine conversion was shown in Liu's lab in 2016 and for adenine in 2017, the latter using a deaminase evolved in the laboratory because no natural DNA adenosine deaminase existed. That is enzyme chemistry done as a design problem, and it is a part of the prize I can defend to a chemist.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection to B039 is still that it reads as a successor to the 2010 prize, and that the committee has to accept that a refinement made general by ligands is itself a prize-level step. The strongest objection to B062 is that it is about ten years old, that clinical results are still accumulating, that Kondo and Nishida's independent 2016 work and Komor's and Gaudelli's first-author roles are not honoured by a Liu-only citation, and that the field is next to the 2020 CRISPR prize. The pairing also has no scientific link between its parts. I have no better answer to that than to say that a chemistry prize can honour two different kinds of chemical achievement, and I would drop the second part sooner than invent a unifying phrase.

responses.point: Heiner asked me to say more about the 2010 overlap, to help word the C-N citation around the bond formed rather than around cross-coupling in general, and to place the Kosugi and Migita precedents chronologically.
responses.response: The wording I now propose is built on the C-N bond, and I have put the chronology in my case: Kosugi and Migita 1983 (stoichiometric tin amides), Buchwald 1994 (catalytic but still tin-dependent), Buchwald and Hartwig 1995 and after (free amines, a base, and ligand-controlled catalysis). The distinction from 2010 is chemical: reductive elimination to form C-N, in competition with beta-hydride elimination, is not what the C-C reactions had to solve. I also correct the record the chair noted: my round-1 reply to the chair referred to nanopore sequencing, which is not on the shortlist and I should not have mentioned. The chair's alternatives are B066 and B036 and my comment on them was meant to refer to those.

responses.point: Johan accepts that Buchwald and Hartwig are the cleanest attribution but asks whether C-N coupling is something completely new, since it refines a bond-forming method already rewarded, and expects a difference of philosophy. He prefers B062 plus B066 with Crews and Handa.
responses.response: I agree that this is a difference of philosophy and I do not think either side is wrong on the facts. My test is whether chemists can do something routinely that they could not do before, rather than whether the idea is the first of its kind. Aryl amines went from a difficult problem to a standard disconnection, and that is a change in capability. I would ask in return whether B066 with Crews and Handa is cleaner than B039: Johan's own text says Deshaies, Ciulli, Sakamoto and Gray were decisive, and no bifunctional degrader appears approved. I keep B066 as an alternative, and if the committee prefers a configuration with B062 plus B066 instead of B039, I would accept it as a second-best case, though I would still favour the cleaner credit of B039.

responses.point: Andrei supports Liu alone in his file but his opening proposal and response text include Komor and Gaudelli, and the chair asked for dated evidence separating the first demonstrations of base editing from the Nishida and Kondo work.
responses.response: My view on dating is that Liu's cytidine base editor (Komor et al., 2016) preceded the independent Target-AID work of Nishida, Kondo and colleagues by a few months, and the adenine editor (Gaudelli et al., 2017) has no counterpart in the Japanese work. Neither establishes that the Kondo and Nishida work was derivative, and it supports calling them independent. With a limit of three names and two parts, I cannot add Komor and Gaudelli without removing someone or dropping a part. I keep Liu alone because he conceived and directed both editors. I would reconsider only if the committee decides on B062 as the only part, in which case Liu, Komor and Gaudelli is the set I would support, and Kondo and Nishida should then be considered seriously too.

responses.point: Emma ranks condensates first and C-N coupling sixth, and in round 1 I asked for a clearer chemical formulation of B036.
responses.response: Her round-1 statement supplied one that I find more persuasive than before: multivalent interactions driving demixing, with Hyman and Brangwynne giving the cellular demonstration and Rosen the in vitro reconstitution, so that the trio maps to three documented steps. I accept that it has a real physical-chemical principle. My remaining reservations are the ones she lists herself: liquid versus gel character is contested for many reported condensates, and Pappu and Mittag fall outside a three-name cut. I do not move it into my configuration but I regard it as a serious case, and I would not oppose it on the grounds that it is not chemistry.

responses.point: Daniel puts targeted protein degradation first with Crews, Deshaies and Handa, and asks whether PROTACs and the cereblon glue mechanism form one achievement.
responses.response: I agree that degradation is the strongest alternative to base editing and I keep B066 as my first alternative. I still see two things in it that are not one discovery: the PROTAC concept and the cereblon mechanism of thalidomide-type drugs, which were joined into a single story afterwards. A single citation would need to say what unites them, and the committee has not agreed on the third name. If B066 is a part of the majority configuration I would support Crews, Deshaies and Handa over a pharmacology-led alternative.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts C-N coupling as a distinct, unrecognised principle after the 2010 prize.
Whether base editing is judged as chemistry or as genome engineering, and whether Liu alone is acceptable given Komor, Gaudelli, Kondo and Nishida.
Whether a two-part prize with no scientific link between the parts is acceptable.
Whether the primary-literature dates I cite for the 2016 and 2017 base-editing papers and for the 1983 to 1995 amination chronology are exactly right; I rely on memory and not on a file I was given.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict or recusal to disclose. I share Lund University with Heiner Linke and Emma Sparr, which is an ordinary colleague connection, and I have no known personal, collaborative or institutional tie to Buchwald, Hartwig, Liu, or any other shortlisted candidate. My own field is synthetic organic chemistry, which could lead me to give C-N coupling more weight than other members do.
